text:
tara: Heads-up from today's bring-up: rnrk-v5-int8 passed NDCG checks but we have a top-1 MRR regression focused on short docs that mix inline code, tables and URLs. Pattern looks distinct from previous newline-only failures.
mike: Can we see a minimal repro from the holdout?
tara: Minimal example:
```
query: "upload to s3 with curl"
doc_good: "Steps:
1) Create presigned URL
2) curl -X PUT -T file.json "$URL"
3) notify via webhook"  -> fp16 rank 1

doc_bad: "Use curl to upload to S3. Example:
| endpoint | example |
|---|---|
| PUT | `curl -X PUT -T file.json https://s3.amazonaws.com/bucket` |
See also https://docs.example.com/s3-upload" -> int8 rank 3
```
eli: Token counts differ: fp16 doc_bad tokens 48, int8 doc_bad tokens 44. Token strings near table cell and URL show mergers: fp16 ['`', 'curl', '-X', 'PUT', 'file.json', 'https', '://', 's3', '.', 'amazonaws', '.', 'com'] vs int8 ['`curl-XPUT', 'file.jsonhttps://s3.amazonaws.com/bucket`']
sam: That looks like a tokenizer config mismatch during packaging or a downstream normalization step collapsing punctuation. Which tokenizer sha was bundled with the quantized artifact?
tara: Packaging log shows tokenizer v2.3.1 but runtime uses v2.3.0 in the container. Oops.
ci-bot: :robot_face: queued job 5201234567-token-diff: ./tools/tokenizer_diff --model rnrk-v5-int8 --slice punct-heavy --samples 800
mike: Immediate mitigations: (1) add a transient preproc that spaces out pipes/backticks/urls before tokenization, (2) pin tokenizer sha in packaging and fail fast if mismatch, (3) run per-head calibration sweep to check attention collapse on punctuation tokens.
eli: Also try a hybrid quant run where attention stays fp16: ./eval --model rnrk-v5-hybrid --slice punct-heavy --samples 1200
tara: I ran a quick local with normalized preproc (insert spaces around | and backticks) on 1k samples: int8+norm recovered ~2.9% of the MRR gap. Hybrid run recovered ~3.6%. Baseline gap was ~4.5%.
mike: Good signal. Per-head calibs might close the last 1% if certain heads are collapsing. Can you dump head-wise attention norms for top mismatches?
ci-bot: :white_check_mark: job 5201234567-token-diff completed: found 31 tokenizer mismatches. Report: https://redwood.internal/tdiff/5201234567
eli: Next steps I propose: A) pin tokenizer and add a packaging parity check, B) run per-head calibration on a 2k sample shard, C) add a golden slice of 600 punct-heavy docs (tables, inline code, urls, monospace) to onboarding CI with assert top1 MRR delta <= 1.5% vs fp16, D) document a temporary normalization preproc for model bringup.
tara: I'll open PRs for the golden slice + CI runner and the preproc. mike, can you own the packaging parity fix?
mike: Yup. I'll add a sha check and a tokenizer-diff smoke test in the release pipeline.
eli: I'll kick off the per-head calibration sweep and the hybrid eval and upload activation dumps to the issue.
sam: Also add a short note to the onboarding checklist: "verify punctuation-heavy slices (tables/code/urls) during quantization".
tara: Thanks. Closing once PRs merge and we get one clean rerun against full holdout.
